$comment: Capability contracts for the shipped skills (C8). Machine-readable on purpose: this is the raw material for MCPHub/SaaS permissioning. Vocabularies and the honesty rule live in src/helpers/skill-capabilities.mjs; `npm run validate` fails the build when this file, the SKILL.md pages, and the code disagree.

auto-mode.summary: Sets the wiki auto-enrichment mode for the session, optionally persisting it to the workspace .env.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill, so nothing proves the page calls what it declares. The write side is narrow and well understood: the only mutation is the router's own mode state, persisted to the workspace .env by the tool itself.

autoresearch.summary: Runs an autonomous web-fed research loop against a written research program until its questions close.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. Two specifics the reader should know. First, the network access is NOT via a router tool but via the host's WebSearch/WebFetch, so no router-side policy sees it. Second, this entry's reads/writes/writeMode are the DELEGATION CLOSURE, not what this page does itself: the vault writes all happen inside wiki-ingest, which is `destructive` (it moves files, and write_bundle has no move step), so the closure is what a permission engine must grant to run autoresearch at all. The validator enforces that dominance rather than trusting the prose. Since v0.69.0 the page also calls find_boundary_pages (C10) in step 0, and only when the user named no topic: it is read-only and adds nothing to the write closure, but it is a real call, not a mention.

build-search-index.summary: Builds or refreshes the vault's local BM25 search index under wiki-meta/search-index.json.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. The tool behind it is well covered (tests/bm25-index.test.mjs) and the only artifact written is regenerable, so a wrong contract here costs a rebuild, not content.

canvas.summary: Creates or rewrites Obsidian .canvas files with auto-layout, always as a whole-file write.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. patch_file appears only as a documented anti-pattern ("don't patch JSON"), which is why it sits in toolsMentionedNotCalled — a reader of the page alone could reasonably conclude the opposite.

conventions.summary: Installs, removes or reports CLAUDE.md convention snippets across vaults.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. The local:fs atoms are real and easy to miss: the snippet library lives in the PLUGIN INSTALL directory, which the skill both globs and (for `add`) writes into — outside every vault and outside the workspace.

decision-consolidate.summary: Compresses a settled decision page to its canon and moves the deliberation chronicle to an archive note.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill, and this one rewrites authored prose in place — the highest-consequence unverified contract in the set. Its guards (refuse on status 'proposed', verify the archive before compressing) are procedural, not enforced by code. Step 6 prescribes re-running the decision lint pass 'via the wiki-lint skill OR the repo script', so BOTH paths are declared: the delegation closure of wiki-lint, and requires.shell. search_smart is prose only — it appears once, to say archives are excluded from that surface — but vault:search stays in reads because the wiki-lint closure genuinely reaches it.

defuddle.summary: Fetches a webpage and returns cleaned markdown plus structured metadata, before ingestion.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. filter_relevant_blocks is explicitly left to the CONSUMER by the page ('don't filter inside defuddle') — the bootstrap read the mention as a call, which is exactly why the generated proposal is not the contract. The page's 'hand off to wiki-ingest' is listed as mentioned-not-invoked rather than a delegation: defuddle is a PREPROCESSOR that wiki-ingest calls, so reading that line as a descent produces a defuddle->wiki-ingest->defuddle cycle. The cycle check is what surfaced the mismodelling.

discover-list-files.summary: Lists files and subdirectories inside a vault directory.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. Thin single-tool wrapper; the residual risk is that a future edit adds a call without updating this entry, which is what the tool-mention check catches.

discover-list-vaults.summary: Lists every configured vault with its online status and metadata.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. Thin single-tool wrapper. `router:config` is listed because list_vaults surfaces the router's own configuration, not just vault contents.

hot-compact.summary: Compacts an oversized wiki-meta/hot.md back to its cache contract, after a verified full backup.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. `shell: true` is not incidental: step 1 tells the operator to reach the vault's Local REST API from a Bash/python script when hot.md is too large to load into context. That path bypasses every router-side guard, so a permission model must see it.

lock.summary: Restricts the router to a single vault for the session, optionally persisting to the workspace .env.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. The only mutation is the router's own lock state; persistence writes the workspace .env via the tool.

manage-delete.summary: Permanently deletes a vault file, behind a two-step preview-then-confirm guard.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. The confirm=true guard IS enforced by the tool (not by the page), but nothing verifies the page honours its own preview-first procedure — the highest-consequence gap in the set alongside decision-consolidate.

manage-move.summary: Moves or renames a vault file via GET source → PUT destination → DELETE source.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. Classed `destructive` rather than `mutating` because the move is not atomic: the Local REST API has no native move, so a failure between PUT and DELETE leaves two copies or none.

meta-attach-vault.summary: Interactive wizard that attaches an Obsidian vault to a code workspace: provision, bind .env, edit .gitignore.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. This is the widest contract in the set: it runs setup-vault.mjs through Bash, can `git init`, and writes four files in the workspace. It also invokes the `conventions` skill, so its reads/writes cover that closure too — the vault:content and local:fs atoms come from there, not from anything this page does itself. The preview-and-explain discipline the page describes is entirely procedural.

meta-audit-bridge-readiness.summary: Read-only audit of click-to-open readiness per vault, including a live probe of the /open route.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. It calls no router tool at all — the work is a CLI script run through Bash, which is why `tools` is empty and `shell` is true. The live probe hits loopback only, so `network` stays false.

meta-setup.summary: Installs obsidian-mcp-router and registers it as the user-scope Obsidian MCP server.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. `network: true` because the documented path clones from GitHub and installs npm dependencies; `local:fs` because it edits ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.claude.json, outside any vault.

meta-status.summary: Read-only diagnostic of the router and every configured vault, with fix suggestions.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. The page states its own read-only contract explicitly ("Don't run write/delete tools as part of this skill"), but that is a written instruction, not an enforced one.

meta-sync-template.summary: Propagates the reference vault's plugins, snippets and root docs to one or more configured vaults.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill — but this is the one entry where the dangerous part IS verified elsewhere: the credential-leak refusal and the self-sync refusal live in setup-vault.mjs and are pinned by tests/setup-vault-safety.test.mjs. The skill layer above them is pure UX and unverified.

obsidian-bases.summary: Creates or edits Obsidian Bases (.base files) — YAML database views over vault notes.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. Writes .base files, which Obsidian executes as live queries — a malformed one degrades a view but cannot lose authored content.

obsidian-markdown.summary: Reference-only syntax guide for Obsidian Flavored Markdown; other skills consult it.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. This one is pure reference — it has no procedure and calls nothing, so the contract is trivially empty and its only failure mode is going stale against Obsidian's syntax.

read-frontmatter.summary: Reads frontmatter (whole object or one key) from a vault file, preserving types.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. Thin single-tool wrapper.

read-get.summary: Reads the full content of a vault file and surfaces its contentSha256 for later conditional writes.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. The five write tools named here appear ONLY in the contentSha256 paragraph, which explains where to replay the hash later — the bootstrap read them as calls and proposed writeMode `destructive` for a pure reader. Corrected by hand; this is the clearest evidence that the generated proposal must never be trusted as-is.

read-search.summary: Plain-text substring search inside a vault, with surrounding context.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. Thin single-tool wrapper; cross-vault fan-out (vault: "*") widens the read surface to every configured vault, which is why a permission model should treat `vault:search` as fleet-wide here.

read-search-smart.summary: Semantic search via Smart Connections embeddings, with an honest fall back to the local BM25 tier.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. The plugin requirement is conditional, not absolute — it binds only the semantic tier; `tier: local` needs nothing but a built index. The declaration lists the maximum, which overstates the requirement rather than the permission, the safe direction.

save.summary: Files the current conversation (or one insight) as a typed, cross-linked wiki note plus its journal line.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. `destructive` rather than `transactional` is deliberate and the validator now enforces it: the page moves files, and `write_bundle` has NO move step (C2 left it out because a half-undone move is worse than no undo), so those calls run outside the transaction. The page also leaves the backlinks step out of the bundle on purpose — its patch→404→append fallback would roll the save back — so one documented write runs unprotected. `router:config` covers the session-journal sidecar it reads from ~/.claude/.

sync-from-github.summary: Syncs one vault or the whole fleet straight from the GitHub skeleton — plugins, themes, snippets, root docs.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill — but the hard parts are verified below it: archive extraction refuses path traversal, NTFS streams and Windows device names (tests/targz-extract.test.mjs), and only a pinned plugin allowlist may be copied from the network. Unverified at this layer: that the skill never passes --repo on its own, which is a written rule and the whole reason a non-default repo also demands --trust-repo.

template-execute.summary: Executes a Templater template, optionally writing the rendered output to a new file.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. `create-only` reflects the documented use (render to a NEW file); note that the template itself is arbitrary user JavaScript run inside Obsidian, so the real reach of this skill is bounded by Templater, not by this contract.

unlock.summary: Lifts the single-vault lock and restores normal multi-vault routing.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. lock_vault is named only to describe what is being undone. Worth flagging for a permission model: unlocking WIDENS the reachable vault set, so it is a privilege-increasing operation despite looking like a cleanup.

who-is-speaking.summary: Identifies the family member for the session on a shared vault, then locks the router and sets the enrich mode.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. It changes routing based on an identity the user asserts in chat — there is no authentication anywhere in this path, and nothing verifies the claimed member.

wiki.summary: Bootstraps the Karpathy-style LLM-wiki structure inside a vault and initialises the OKF projections.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. Classed `destructive` because the scaffolding step relocates misplaced files with move_file. `local:fs` covers reading templates/wiki/CLAUDE.md from the plugin install directory, outside the vault.

wiki-boundary.summary: Ranks the wiki's "frontier" pages — heavily linked, thin inside — from the persisted knowledge graph.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. The reach is genuinely one read: find_boundary_pages makes a single get_file call for wiki-meta/graph/knowledge-graph.json and computes the rest in memory — pinned by a test that asserts the exact call list. build_wiki_graph is named only in the recovery advice ("graph missing or too old → offer /wiki-graph") and search_smart only in the explanation of what autoresearch already does on its own; declaring either as called would make a pure reader look like a writer.

wiki-export.summary: Exports the wiki as an llms.txt file or a conformant OKF v0.1 bundle under wiki-meta/exports/.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. `cache` because output lands only under wiki-meta/exports/ and is regenerable — the page states the wiki itself is never mutated, but that is a written rule and it writes with the same general-purpose write_file as everything else.

wiki-fold.summary: Rolls up journal entries into a structurally-idempotent fold page with backlinks to its children.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. Its idempotency contract is enforced by hand (fetch, normalise, compare) rather than by the router; the programmatic equivalent, contentIsUnchanged in src/helpers/wiki-fingerprint.mjs, is tested but is not what this skill runs.

wiki-graph.summary: Builds a typed knowledge graph from the wiki and writes it under wiki-meta/graph/.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. The graph build itself is deterministic and tested (tests/wiki-graph-builder.test.mjs); everything written is regenerable from the wiki.

wiki-ingest.summary: Ingests a source (URL, file or pasted text) into the wiki as cross-referenced pages, recording the source.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. The BATCH path runs inside agents/wiki-ingest.md, whose tool allowlist the harness does enforce — but the ordinary in-process path is bound by nothing, so no tier above `declared` would be true for the skill as a whole. `destructive` rather than `transactional`: it calls move_file, and write_bundle has no move step, so that call sits outside the rollback. list_files, merge_frontmatter, search and search_smart are declared because that agent grants them, even though the page never names them — the agent-allowlist cross-check surfaced the gap.

wiki-lint.summary: Health-checks the wiki (orphans, dead links, index drift, frontmatter gaps); read-only unless --fix is asked for.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. Declared `mutating` for the MAXIMUM reachable state (--fix-errors applies set_frontmatter), not the default posture, which is read-only. refresh_okf_projections is called with check:true only — read-only in practice — but this schema cannot express "this tool, only in its read mode", so `vault:derived` is declared as a write: overstating the reach is the safe direction, understating it is not. record_source is named only to say lint must never write the ledger. Since v0.69.0 Check A-ter calls find_boundary_pages (C10) — read-only, reported at info tier only, so it widens neither the write set nor writeMode. Since v0.72.0 Check J-bis calls find_twin_pages (C11) — read-only, filesystem-only, reported at info tier only, so it widens neither the write set nor writeMode.

wiki-neighbors.summary: Shows a page's graph neighbours — forward links, backlinks, or both, at a configurable hop depth.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. The three extra tools are named only in error-recovery advice ("graph missing → offer to run /wiki-graph"); the bootstrap proposed writeMode `cache` from them, which would have made a pure reader look like a writer.

wiki-path.summary: Finds the shortest chain of links between two wiki pages from the persisted knowledge graph.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. Thin single-tool wrapper over a deterministic graph lookup; it reads only the persisted graph, never the pages.

wiki-query.summary: Answers a question grounded in the existing vault via three-tier retrieval, without fetching the web.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. The "no web fetching" property that distinguishes this from autoresearch is a written rule, not an enforced one — nothing stops the model from reaching for WebFetch mid-answer.

wiki-refresh-digests.summary: Regenerates stale or missing digest sidecars under wiki-meta/digests/.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill, AND this contract's write side is inferred rather than read: the page describes writing digests ("serialise and write to digestPathForPage") without ever naming the write tool, so get_file and write_file are declared from how the skill must work, not from what it says. That gap is itself worth fixing in the page.

wiki-tour.summary: Generates a guided reading tour through a vault, ordered deterministically from the graph topology.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. `create-only` because the tour lands as a new standalone page; the build_wiki_tour tool also updates the graph's tour[] field, which is derived data.

write-append.summary: Appends content at the end of a vault file, auto-creating it unless requireExisting is set.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. `append-only` is accurate for the tool but note it auto-creates missing files, so it is not purely additive to an existing corpus. write_file is named only as the contrast case.

write-bundle.summary: Runs several vault writes as one journaled all-or-nothing operation; also the crash-recovery entry point.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill — but this is the least worrying entry in the set, because write_bundle executes its steps THROUGH the existing tools and their guards, and the underlying transaction is heavily pinned (tests/write-bundle.test.mjs, tests/write-bundle-integration.test.mjs). The six tools in toolsMentionedNotCalled are step KINDS the skill passes as data, not calls it makes; the effective write surface is therefore all of them, which is what `writes` records.

write-create-or-replace.summary: Creates a new vault file or replaces an existing one entirely, with ifNew / ifMatch guards.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. The ifMatch precondition IS enforced by the tool and the bridge (tests/if-match-writes.test.mjs), but nothing makes this skill USE it — the page's overwrite-confirm discipline is procedural.

write-frontmatter-merge.summary: Applies several frontmatter updates to one file in a single call.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. `transactional` only when the page routes through write_bundle, which is what makes merge_frontmatter all-or-nothing since v0.66.0; called directly, the tool is still sequential and reports partial failures per key.

write-frontmatter-set.summary: Sets or replaces a single frontmatter property, preserving types.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. Thin single-tool wrapper; type inference from the user's phrasing happens in the skill layer and is exactly the unverified part.

write-patch.summary: Surgical edit — inserts or replaces under a heading, block id or frontmatter key.

verification.reason: No harness executes a skill. The heading-full-path rule the page teaches (H1::H2::H3, not the bare leaf) is the kind of thing that fails at runtime with invalid-target and is checked by nothing here. The two other write tools are named as fallbacks for the 404 case.
